values.name: Const_00
values.desc: Resetting bit INIT enables the participation of the node in the CAN traffic. If the CAN node is in the bus-off state, the ongoing bus-off recovery (which does not depend on the INIT bit) is continued. With the end of the bus-off recovery sequence the CAN node is allowed to take part in the CAN traffic. If the CAN node is not in the bus-off state, a sequence of 11 consecutive recessive bits must be detected before the node is allowed to take part in the CAN traffic.

values.name: Const_01
values.desc: Setting this bit terminates the participation of this node in the CAN traffic. Any ongoing frame transfer is cancelled and the transmit line goes recessive. If the CAN node is in the bus-off state, then the running bus-off recovery sequence is continued. If the INIT bit is still set after the successful completion of the bus-off recovery sequence, i.e. after detecting 128 sequences of 11 consecutive recessive bits (11 1), then the CAN node leaves the bus-off state but remains inactive as long as INIT remains set.

values.name: Const_00
values.desc: Message object n accepts the reception of both, standard and extended frames.

values.name: Const_01

fields.name: ID
fields.desc: CAN Identifier of Message Object n

fields.name: IDE
fields.desc: Identifier Extension Bit of Message Object n

values.name: Const_00
values.desc: Message object n handles standard frames with 11-bit identifier.

values.name: Const_01
values.desc: Message object n handles extended frames with 29-bit identifier.

values.name: Const_01
values.desc: Transmit acceptance filtering is based on the list order. This means that message object n is considered for transmission only if there is no other message object with valid transmit request (MSGVAL & TXEN0 & TXEN1 = 1) somewhere before this object in the list.

values.name: Const_02
values.desc: Transmit acceptance filtering is based on the CAN identifier. This means, message object n is considered for transmission only if there is no other message object with higher priority identifier + IDE + DIR (with respect to CAN arbitration rules) somewhere in the list (see ).

values.name: Const_03
values.desc: Transmit acceptance filtering is based on the list order (as PRI = 01B).

fields.name: IDE
fields.desc: Identifier Extension Bit of Message Object n

values.name: Const_00
values.desc: Message object n handles standard frames with 11-bit identifier.

values.name: Const_01
values.desc: Message object n handles extended frames with 29-bit identifier.

values.name: Const_01
values.desc: Transmit acceptance filtering is based on the list order. This means that message object n is considered for transmission only if there is no other message object with valid transmit request (MSGVAL & TXEN0 & TXEN1 = 1) somewhere before this object in the list.

values.name: Const_02
values.desc: Transmit acceptance filtering is based on the CAN identifier. This means, message object n is considered for transmission only if there is no other message object with higher priority identifier + IDE + DIR (with respect to CAN arbitration rules) somewhere in the list (see ).

values.name: Const_03
values.desc: Transmit acceptance filtering is based on the list order (as PRI = 01B).

values.name: Const_00
values.desc: Message object n handles standard frames with 11-bit identifier.

values.name: Const_01
values.desc: Message object n handles extended frames with 29-bit identifier.

values.name: Const_01
values.desc: Transmit acceptance filtering is based on the list order. This means that message object n is considered for transmission only if there is no other message object with valid transmit request (MSGVAL & TXEN0 & TXEN1 = 1) somewhere before this object in the list.

values.name: Const_02
values.desc: Transmit acceptance filtering is based on the CAN identifier. This means, message object n is considered for transmission only if there is no other message object with higher priority identifier + IDE + DIR (with respect to CAN arbitration rules) somewhere in the list (see ).

values.name: Const_03
values.desc: Transmit acceptance filtering is based on the list order (as PRI = 01B).

values.name: Const_00
values.desc: Resetting bit INIT enables the participation of the node in the CAN traffic. If the CAN node is in the bus-off state, the ongoing bus-off recovery (which does not depend on the INIT bit) is continued. With the end of the bus-off recovery sequence the CAN node is allowed to take part in the CAN traffic. If the CAN node is not in the bus-off state, a sequence of 11 consecutive recessive bits must be detected before the node is allowed to take part in the CAN traffic.

values.name: Const_01
values.desc: Setting this bit terminates the participation of this node in the CAN traffic. Any ongoing frame transfer is cancelled and the transmit line goes recessive. If the CAN node is in the bus-off state, then the running bus-off recovery sequence is continued. If the INIT bit is still set after the successful completion of the bus-off recovery sequence, i.e. after detecting 128 sequences of 11 consecutive recessive bits (11 1), then the CAN node leaves the bus-off state but remains inactive as long as INIT remains set.

fields.name: ID
fields.desc: CAN Identifier of Message Object n

fields.name: IDE
fields.desc: Identifier Extension Bit of Message Object n

values.name: Const_00
values.desc: Message object n handles standard frames with 11-bit identifier.

values.name: Const_01
values.desc: Message object n handles extended frames with 29-bit identifier.

values.name: Const_01
values.desc: Transmit acceptance filtering is based on the list order. This means that message object n is considered for transmission only if there is no other message object with valid transmit request (MSGVAL & TXEN0 & TXEN1 = 1) somewhere before this object in the list.

values.name: Const_02
values.desc: Transmit acceptance filtering is based on the CAN identifier. This means, message object n is considered for transmission only if there is no other message object with higher priority identifier + IDE + DIR (with respect to CAN arbitration rules) somewhere in the list (see ).

values.name: Const_03
values.desc: Transmit acceptance filtering is based on the list order (as PRI = 01B).

values.name: Const_00
values.desc: Message object n handles standard frames with 11-bit identifier.

values.name: Const_01
values.desc: Message object n handles extended frames with 29-bit identifier.

values.name: Const_01
values.desc: Transmit acceptance filtering is based on the list order. This means that message object n is considered for transmission only if there is no other message object with valid transmit request (MSGVAL & TXEN0 & TXEN1 = 1) somewhere before this object in the list.

values.name: Const_02
values.desc: Transmit acceptance filtering is based on the CAN identifier. This means, message object n is considered for transmission only if there is no other message object with higher priority identifier + IDE + DIR (with respect to CAN arbitration rules) somewhere in the list (see ).

values.name: Const_03
values.desc: Transmit acceptance filtering is based on the list order (as PRI = 01B).

values.name: Const_00
values.desc: UNDEFINED. Wakeup not yet executed by the Communication Controller.

values.name: Const_01
values.desc: RECEIVED_HEADER. Set when the Communication Controller finishes wakeup due to the reception of a Frame Header without coding violation on either channel in “WAKEUP_LISTEN” state.

values.name: Const_02
values.desc: RECEIVED_WUP. Set when the Communication Controller finishes wakeup due to the reception of a valid wakeup pattern on the configured wakeup channel in “WAKEUP_LISTEN” state.

values.name: Const_03
values.desc: COLLISION_HEADER. Set when the Communication Controller stops wakeup due to a detected collision during wakeup pattern transmission by receiving a valid Header on either channel.

values.name: Const_04
values.desc: COLLISION_WUP. Set when the Communication Controller stops wakeup due to a detected collision during wakeup pattern transmission by receiving a valid wakeup pattern on the configured wakeup channel.

values.name: Const_05
values.desc: COLLISION_UNKNOWN. Set when the Communication Controller stops wakeup by leaving “WAKEUP_DETECT” state after expiration of the wakeup timer without receiving a valid wakeup pattern or a valid Frame Header.

values.name: Const_06
values.desc: TRANSMITTED. Set when the Communication Controller has successfully completed the transmission of the wakeup pattern.
